figures.cap: plank of 9.6 m at 10 degrees to ground resting on a ramp inclined at 60 degrees; x along ramp

solutions.latex:
The angle in the triangle beside the ramp angle is supplementary: $180 - 60 = 120^\circ$.

Using the sine rule:
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 10^\circ} = \dfrac{9.6}{\sin 120^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{9.6 \sin 10^\circ}{\sin 120^\circ} \\ &\approx 1.9 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Sets up the sine rule, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
In the triangle given below, calculate the length of $x$ correct to 1 decimal place.

\exfigure{719_q20_1}

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} x^2 &= 28^2 + 22^2 - 2 \times 28 \times 22 \times \cos 97^\circ \\ x &= \sqrt{28^2 + 22^2 - 2 \times 28 \times 22 \times \cos 97^\circ} \\ &= 37.658\ldots \\ &\approx 37.7 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

Using the sine rule,

figures.cap: triangle with sides 5 and x, angles 105 and 20 degrees

parts.latex:
Which calculation could be used to find the value of $x$ in this triangle?

\exfigure{716_q4_1}

solutions.latex:
The side $x$ is opposite $105^\circ$ and the side $5$ is opposite $20^\circ$, so use the sine rule.

$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 105^\circ} = \dfrac{5}{\sin 20^\circ}$$

$$x = \dfrac{5 \times \sin 105^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ}$$

Hence the answer is option D.

figures.cap: triangle with sides 11 cm and x cm, angles 95 and 60

parts.latex: Calculate the value of $x$, correct to two significant figures.
Calculate the area of the triangle to the nearest square centimetre.

solutions.latex:
The angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$, so the third angle is
$$180^\circ-95^\circ-60^\circ=25^\circ$$
Using the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 60^\circ}=\dfrac{11}{\sin 25^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{11\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 25^\circ} \\ &= 23 \text{ cm (2 s.f.)} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct rearranged expression for $x$, or equivalent merit
Correct application of the sine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula $A=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ with the included angle $95^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 11\times 22.54\ldots\times\sin 95^\circ \\ &= 123.5\ldots \\ &\approx 124 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct substitution into the area formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Town $B$ is 125 km due west of town $C$

Town $A$ is on a bearing $036^\circ$ from $B$ and on a bearing $320^\circ$ from $C$.

\exfigure{827_q12_1}

Which calculation could be used to find the distance from $A$ to $B$?

solutions.latex:
Use the angles at $B$ and $C$ from the bearings.

$$\begin{aligned} \angle C &= 320^\circ-270^\circ=50^\circ \\ \angle B &= 90^\circ-36^\circ=54^\circ \\ \angle A &= 180^\circ-50^\circ-54^\circ=76^\circ \end{aligned}$$

By the sine rule, $AB$ is opposite $\angle C$ and $BC$ is opposite $\angle A$.

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{AB}{\sin50^\circ} &= \dfrac{125}{\sin76^\circ} \\ AB &= \dfrac{125\sin50^\circ}{\sin76^\circ} \end{aligned}$$

Hence the correct option is the one with $\dfrac{125\sin50^\circ}{\sin76^\circ}$.

Drawn angles follow the crop (rule 1).

figures.cap: triangle of campsites A, B, C with north arrow

parts.latex: Calculate the length of the road between B and C, correct to 4 significant figures.
Hence, or otherwise, find the area of the triangle enclosed by the 3 roads, correct to the nearest square metre.

solutions.latex:
At $A$, the angle between the bearings of $B$ and $C$ is
$$\angle CAB = 209^\circ - 125^\circ = 84^\circ$$
The bearing of $A$ from $C$ is $209^\circ - 180^\circ = 29^\circ$, so
$$\angle ACB = 85^\circ - 29^\circ = 56^\circ$$
By the sine rule in triangle $ABC$:
$$\dfrac{BC}{\sin 84^\circ} = \dfrac{8.7}{\sin 56^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} BC &= 8.7 \times \dfrac{\sin 84^\circ}{\sin 56^\circ} \\ &= 10.44 \text{ km} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ BC = 10.44 \text{ km}$$
criteria: Finds the 2 correct angles inside the diagram and attempts to use the sine rule, or equivalent merit
Finds $\angle CAB$ or the bearing of $A$ from $C$, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: Rounding is not important in this part.
meta.format_note: Diagram of triangle with bearings would help; source has the question's figure only.

solutions.latex:
The angle sum of triangle $ABC$ gives
$$\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 84^\circ - 56^\circ = 40^\circ$$
Using the area formula:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \dfrac{1}{2}(10.4366\ldots)(8.7)\sin 40^\circ \\ &= 29.182\,073\ldots \text{ km}^2 \\ &= 29\,182\,073 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{area} \approx 29\,182\,073 \text{ m}^2$$
criteria: Finds the angle $ABC$, or attempts to use the area formula, or equivalent merit
